readings: replace the elevation of those n nodes with values read from the Mapbox DEM (intended)
replace those n nodes themselves with a DEM layer
replace those n elevation values with the Mapbox DEM as a data source setting
entries.resolution: English: 'Replace the elevation of those {n} nodes with values from the Mapbox DEM?'

entries.complaint: medium: 'the nodes that will be filled in' says the NODES are filled, not their elevations. In a drawing application 'filled in' is also what happens to a shape, and this string is read next to a map. Same shape in lpn_terrain_filled_ids.
readings: these nodes will have their elevation written from the DEM (intended)
these nodes will be drawn filled or shaded
these nodes will be completed in some unspecified way
entries.resolution: English: 'These nodes will get an elevation: {ids}'. And lpn_terrain_filled_ids: 'These nodes got an elevation: {ids}'.

entries.complaint: medium: 'still blank' has no noun. A node is not blank; its elevation is. A translator with no antecedent in the string will attach blankness to the node, which in a map editor reads as unlabelled or empty rather than missing a number.
readings: these nodes still have no elevation (intended)
these nodes are empty or unnamed
these nodes were not drawn
entries.resolution: English: 'These nodes still have no elevation: {ids}'

entries.complaint: medium: 'They are: {ids}' is pure anaphora with the antecedent in a different key (lpn_terrain_keep, which is not in this batch). Every gendered language must choose a gender and number for 'they' with nothing to choose from, and the two candidates in the surrounding paragraph are nodes and elevations.
readings: the nodes that already have an elevation and will not be touched (intended)
the elevations that will be kept
the nodes that will be filled in, if the reader misattaches the sentence
entries.resolution: English: 'Those nodes are: {ids}'

entries.complaint: medium: 'better than a metre across the ground and a few tenths of a metre up and down' is the string's only statement of what accuracy means, and it invents a phrasing for two quantities that already have names. 'Across the ground' can be horizontal position, horizontal resolution or ground sample distance, and a reader deciding whether to trust a DEM for a pipe profile needs the vertical number specifically.
readings: about 1 m horizontal and a few tenths of a metre vertical accuracy (intended)
1 m ground resolution, i.e. pixel size, with a separate vertical figure
accuracy measured along the ground surface, as opposed to along the line of sight
entries.resolution: English: replace both pairs with 'horizontally' and 'vertically': 'it can be better than a metre horizontally and a few tenths of a metre vertically. Where only global data exists it is about 30 m horizontally and several metres vertically.' (This string also carries two em dashes; if it is being edited anyway, the ratchet says drop them.)

entries.complaint: medium: Two problems in one sentence. 'its residual pressure' reads as a property the junction has, when it is a criterion the user typed into the dialog; and 'Test every junction' is false whenever the scope is set to the selected junction only, which is one of the two values of the very first control in that dialog.
readings: hold the residual pressure you specified for the run (intended)
hold the residual pressure that this junction has
every junction is always tested, with no choice of scope
entries.resolution: English: 'Test junctions one at a time: how much can each deliver while still holding the residual pressure you set, and does drawing the required flow there push anything else out of limits?'

entries.complaint: medium: 'your code' is a polysemy trap of the first order. Standing alone in a hydraulics tool it is as readable as software code or a postal/area code as it is as a fire code, and several target languages have no word that covers the regulatory sense without a qualifier. 'at a hydrant' also floats: it can qualify the flow or the requirement.
readings: the fire code that applies to your project (intended)
a code you wrote, a program
a reference code or number identifying something
entries.resolution: English: 'The flow your fire code or your fire authority requires at a hydrant. Each junction is tested against this number unless it carries a required fire flow of its own.'

entries.complaint: medium: 'this junction alone must provide' has two readings and one of them is a claim about hydraulics, not about scope. It means 'this junction in particular', but reads just as naturally as 'this junction unaided', which would be a statement that no other part of the network contributes. The second sentence also names 'the Fire flow box', a control whose visible label is 'Required fire flow'.
readings: the requirement that applies to this junction in particular (intended)
the flow this junction must supply without help from the rest of the system
the flow available at this junction on its own
entries.resolution: English: 'The fire flow required at this particular junction, from your fire code or your fire authority for the land use it serves. Leave it blank and the junction is tested against the number in the Required fire flow box.'

entries.complaint: high: As written, the tip's subject is the wrong quantity. '20 psi is the ... convention for available fire flow' says 20 psi IS a fire flow, which is a category error a translator will faithfully reproduce; and it never says what the number is for, which is the residual pressure held while the available flow is measured. It also hardcodes psi in a field whose unit selector may be showing kPa or bar, with no SI value beside it.
readings: 20 psi is the residual pressure conventionally held when measuring available fire flow (intended)
20 psi is the conventional required fire flow
20 psi is the pressure at which fire flow becomes available
entries.resolution: English: 'The pressure the junction must still hold while delivering the fire flow. AWWA M31 and NFPA 291 use 20 psi (140 kPa).'

entries.complaint: medium: 'Design check (effect on system)' names the whole system where the check deliberately excludes the junction under test, and the JS fallback beside it says 'Effect on the rest of the system'. 'Design check' can also be read as the name of the result rather than of the setting, which matters because this label sits on a selector whose values are 'Do not check' and two scopes.
readings: choose whether, and over what set, to check the effect on the REST of the system (intended)
a check of the design of the system as a whole, this junction included
the design check result
entries.resolution: English: 'Design check (effect on the rest of the system)'.

entries.complaint: medium: 'run too fast' uses 'run' for fluid velocity on a page where Run and Runs are already the names of a control and a results column. A translator who has just rendered the Runs heading will read this as something about the analysis running.
readings: exceed the velocity limit you set (intended)
take too long / execute too quickly, i.e. about the analysis
operate outside its design condition generally
entries.resolution: English: '... does anything else fall below its minimum pressure or exceed its velocity limit? Choosing to check it costs no extra calculation.'

entries.complaint: medium: 'Every other junction' is one of the best known ambiguities in English: each of the remaining ones, or alternating ones. As a scope selector for a design check, the wrong reading changes what the report is understood to cover, and the string carries no context that rules it out.
readings: all junctions except the one being tested (intended)
every second junction, alternating
entries.resolution: English: 'All other junctions'. Same fix in lpn_ff_design_all and in lpn_ff_menu_tip if that wording is reused.

entries.complaint: medium: Same 'every other' ambiguity as lpn_ff_design_nodes, compounded because 'every pipe' beside it is unambiguously distributive, which invites the reader to hunt for a contrast in 'every other'.
readings: all other junctions and all pipes (intended)
every second junction, and every pipe
entries.resolution: English: 'All other junctions and all pipes'.

entries.complaint: medium: Two words carry the sentence and both are traps. 'its lateral' is US water-industry shorthand for the service or hydrant lateral and is a bare adjective in most languages; and 'it is the usual one' is a claim about practice sitting next to 'That is the method used here', so the two sentences can be read as one claim or two.
readings: the hydrant lateral pipe is not modelled (intended)
lateral as a direction: sideways losses
the usual one refers to the hydrant rather than to the method
entries.resolution: English: 'Fire flow is drawn at the junction itself, which is the usual method. The hydrant, its lateral pipe and its nozzle are not modelled, so a real hydrant delivers less than the flow shown here.'

entries.complaint: high: Two sentences, and the reader cannot tell whether the second describes what this tool did or what the reader should do. 'Fire flow is normally added to maximum day demand' is advice about practice, printed directly under a statement about the run, so it reads as a description of the run itself. A user who takes that reading believes the sweep was made at maximum day demand when it was made at whatever time step is on screen, and reports a fire flow that was never tested.
readings: standard practice is max day demand, so set that condition yourself before running (intended)
this run adds the fire flow to maximum day demand
maximum day demand is normally added on top of the fire flow
entries.resolution: English: 'Only the time step now on screen is tested. Fire flow is normally tested on top of maximum day demand, so set the network to that condition before you run.'

entries.complaint: medium: 'What is below is what had already been worked out' uses 'below' spatially in a document whose contents are pressures and flows, where below is a magnitude. It is also a headless relative clause twice over, which several target languages cannot mirror without inventing a noun.
readings: the results shown further down the page are the ones already finished (intended)
the results under some threshold value are the finished ones
what remains is what had been computed, i.e. the rest was discarded
entries.resolution: English: 'Stopped after {done} of {total} junctions. The results below are the ones already finished.'

entries.complaint: medium: '{solves} network runs.' is a bare noun phrase punctuated as a sentence, with no verb to tell a translator whether it is a report of what happened, a forecast, or a heading. 'Runs' is also the plural noun of the page's Calculate action rather than of any control named Run.
readings: this sweep took N solves of the whole network (intended)
N network runs will be needed
a label meaning number of network runs
entries.resolution: English: 'This run solved the whole network {solves} times.'

entries.complaint: medium: Three sentences, each beginning with a bare number and no noun. Translators must supply the noun (junctions) to inflect anything, and they cannot see it. Worse, the three counts are deliberately NOT exclusive (js/lpn-fireflow.js counts modes independently), so a language that renders them as a partition, which the parallel form invites, states something false about the run.
readings: N junctions had nothing wrong, N failed the fire flow, N affected the rest of the system, and the sets overlap (intended)
the three counts partition the junctions tested
the counts are of something other than junctions, e.g. of checks
entries.resolution: English: '{clean} junctions had nothing wrong. {fire} junctions failed the fire flow. {design} junctions affected the rest of the system. A junction can appear in more than one of the last two.'

entries.complaint: medium: Same headless count, plus 'could not be answered' predicated of junctions rather than of questions. A junction is not answered; its fire flow question is.
readings: N junctions produced no answer (intended)
N questions could not be answered
N junctions did not respond, i.e. a network or engine failure
entries.resolution: English: '{n} junctions could not be answered.'

entries.complaint: medium: Read as a heading it means 'the junctions that were tested'; read as a sentence, which is how a heading with a past participle scans in several languages, it claims every junction WAS tested. That claim is false when the scope was the selected junction only, and false again past 200 rows, which is the same table's own truncation limit.
readings: the junctions that were tested (intended)
every junction in the project was tested
an instruction: test every junction
entries.resolution: English: 'Junctions tested'.

entries.complaint: medium: The column reports the pressure at the junction with the network's ordinary demands running and no fire flow drawn. That is the fire-test sense of static pressure and is correct usage, but the general hydraulic sense of static is no flow anywhere, and nothing in the table says which is meant. A reader on the wrong sense treats the number as a no-demand pressure, which is always higher.
readings: pressure before the fire flow is drawn, with normal demands running (intended)
pressure with no flow anywhere in the system
static as in a static, non time varying result
entries.resolution: Keep the heading (AWWA M31 and NFPA 291 both call it static pressure) and route the concept to glossary.json: 'static pressure (fire flow): the pressure at the hydrant or junction before any fire flow is drawn, with the system's other demands still running. Not a zero flow pressure.' Every language then anchors on the fire-test sense.

entries.complaint: medium: 'Available flow' drops the word that makes it a term of art. In a hydraulic results table beside velocities and pressures, available flow reads as the flow presently available in the pipes. The paired heading lpn_ff_col_required has the same shape and inherits the same reading.
readings: available fire flow: the largest fire flow that still holds the residual (intended)
the flow currently available at this junction
spare capacity in the pipes serving it
entries.resolution: English: 'Available fire flow' and 'Required fire flow' if the column can take it. If width forbids it, keep the short heads and give both a gloss: pointer to a glossary.json entry for 'available fire flow', so the concept and not the two words is what gets translated.

entries.complaint: medium: 'Residual held' is a participle with its condition removed. The cell holds the pressure the junction still had while delivering the available flow, and neither the word pressure nor the flow it was held at is in the string. A translator gets an adjective and a past participle and no noun.
readings: the residual pressure still present at the available flow (intended)
whether the residual criterion was met, i.e. a yes or no
residual as leftover: the flow left over
entries.resolution: English: 'Residual at available flow' if the column takes it, otherwise 'Residual pressure' with a $ec_lang_syn entry (proposal only, human approval required): 'Residual pressure held while delivering the available fire flow; pressure still standing at the available flow. | layout: column heading'

entries.complaint: medium: 'Pressure at required' ends on an adjective with its noun deleted. English readers recover 'flow' from the neighbouring column; a translator working down a key list has a 50/50 chance of recovering 'required pressure' instead, which inverts the column into the criterion it is being compared against.
readings: the pressure at the junction when the required fire flow is drawn (intended)
the pressure required at the junction
pressure measured at the required condition, unspecified
entries.resolution: English: 'Pressure at required flow'.

entries.complaint: high: The heading names one physical effect and the column reports two. ffCriticalText() prints either a junction pulled below the minimum pressure OR a pipe running above the maximum velocity, and a fast pipe is not a drawdown by any reading of the word. 'Drawdown' additionally carries a specific groundwater meaning (decline of a well water level) that most target languages have a dedicated and wrong word for.
readings: the worst thing this junction pulled down or drove too fast (intended)
the drop in pressure at other junctions only
well drawdown, in the groundwater sense
entries.resolution: English: 'Worst effect', which is true of both cells and of the column's own purpose (the competitor's Critical Asset). Second choice: 'Most affected'.

entries.complaint: high: Same error, in a sentence rather than a heading: 'Nothing in the chosen set was drawn down by any junction tested' is printed whenever the effects list is empty, and that list holds over-velocity pipes as well as low-pressure junctions. If any pipe HAD been over velocity the sentence would not print, so as worded the page says nothing about velocity at all while claiming the design check found nothing.
readings: no junction was pushed below the minimum pressure and no pipe above the maximum velocity (intended)
no pressures were reduced, which says nothing about velocities
drawn down in the groundwater sense
entries.resolution: English: 'Nothing in the chosen set went outside its limits while any junction drew its fire flow.'

entries.complaint: medium: The heading says 'Design limit' and the cells say 'Pressure', 'Velocity', 'Pressure and velocity' or 'Not checked'. A limit is a number; these cells are the name of the limit that was broken. Heading and content are different parts of speech, so a translator will render the heading as the numeric criterion and the reader will look for a value.
readings: which design limit was exceeded (intended)
the value of the design limit applied
the limit imposed by the design of the system
entries.resolution: English: 'Limit exceeded'.

entries.complaint: medium: 'Static failed' turns an adjective into a bare noun and drops the criterion. Nothing static failed; the junction was already below the residual pressure with no fire flow drawn. 'Static' alone also has an everyday electrical and radio sense that several languages will reach for first.
readings: the static pressure was already below the residual, so nothing further was measured (intended)
a static analysis failed
static as in interference or as in unchanging
entries.resolution: English: 'Static pressure already failed, so not checked'. If the cell can take more: 'Below the residual before any fire flow, so not checked'.

entries.complaint: medium: The heading 'Runs' counts solves of the whole network. On this page 'run' is also the name of an extended period simulation, the fire flow sweep is called a run in three other strings in this same batch, and in waterworks English a run of pipe is a length of it. In a table whose first column is Junction, a reader can plausibly take Runs as pipe runs.
readings: the number of times the whole network was solved for this junction (intended)
the number of simulation runs the project has made
runs of pipe serving the junction
entries.resolution: English: 'Network runs'. If the column is too narrow for two words, 'Solves' is unambiguous here even though it was struck as a heading elsewhere; 'Network runs' is preferred.

entries.complaint: medium: A cell containing the single word 'Fire' under the heading 'Failure modes'. It means the junction failed its fire flow criterion. Alone it is the noun for combustion, and every target language will translate the noun. Tom chose the two one-word modes deliberately (2026-09-02), so the English should stand and the translator needs the missing half in the synonym channel.
readings: failed the fire flow criterion (intended)
fire, the thing that burns
a fire condition or fire event
entries.resolution: English kept on Tom's ruling. entries.complaint: medium: 'Design' alone in a cell, meaning the junction's fire flow pushed something else outside its design limits. As a bare word it is a noun and a verb and names an activity rather than a failure.

entries.complaint: medium: 'over {flow}' is two words with no verb, printed in the Available fire flow cell when the search hit its ceiling. 'Over' is one of the most overloaded prepositions in English and none of its senses is marked here: greater than, across, during, or finished.
readings: more than {flow}: the search ceiling was reached and the residual still held (intended)
over as in during or across a period
over as in finished, the run ended at that flow
entries.resolution: English: 'more than {flow}'.

entries.complaint: medium: '{id} down to {pressure}' is telegraphic and verbless. 'Down to' can mean reduced to, or as far as, or attributable to, and the last of those makes the cell read as an explanation of blame rather than a measurement. The companion lpn_ff_affect_link ('{id} at {velocity}') has the same problem in milder form.
readings: junction {id} was pulled down to {pressure} (intended)
the effect goes as far as {id}, at pressure {pressure}
it comes down to {id}, i.e. {id} is the cause
entries.resolution: English: '{id} drops to {pressure}', and for the link string '{id} reaches {velocity}'.

entries.complaint: high: ONE string, TWO different nouns, which CLAUDE.md forbids by name (reuse stops at sentences; a shared string must be true of all its uses). js/looped-network.js appends it to the Drawdowns cell where {n} counts affected junctions and pipes, and again as the line under the table where {n} counts junctions not printed. Every gendered or case-marking language must pick one noun to agree with, so one of the two call sites will be wrong in most of the 26.
readings: and n more affected elements (call site 1)
and n more junctions not shown (call site 2)
and n more of whatever the reader last saw
entries.resolution: Split the key. Proposal: keep lpn_ff_more for the cell as 'and {n} more affected', and add lpn_ff_rows_more for the table footer as '{n} more junctions are not shown.' A new key costs 26 translations; a wrong agreement costs a wrong report in 26 languages.

entries.complaint: high: 'ISO' here is the Insurance Services Office, a US fire insurance rating organisation. Worldwide, and to every one of the 26 translators, ISO means the International Organization for Standardization, which publishes no fire flow hydrant credit. Nothing in the string disambiguates it, so the sentence will be translated as an international standard and read as one, which is a false attribution printed on a deliverable.
readings: the Insurance Services Office, the US fire insurance rating body (intended)
the International Organization for Standardization
an ISO standard number that was omitted
entries.resolution: English: 'The Insurance Services Office (ISO) credits a single hydrant with at most {flow}. That credit limit has not been applied here because we do not know how many hydrants a node may represent.' Consider a glossary.json entry so the expansion, not the acronym, is what travels.

entries.complaint: high: 'with nothing drawn' is false on its face: the network's ordinary demands are still running, and only the fire flow is absent. The key's own name says at_rest, which points at the same wrong idea. A user reading it as no demand at all concludes the network cannot hold the residual even empty, which is a far more alarming diagnosis than the true one.
readings: already below the residual before any FIRE FLOW is drawn, with normal demands running (intended)
already below the residual with no demand at all anywhere
at rest meaning the network is not being simulated
entries.resolution: English: 'Already below the residual before any fire flow is drawn'.

entries.complaint: medium: The placeholder is named {id} and holds a solver ERROR CODE (js/looped-network.js substitutes rec.code). Every other {id} in this batch holds an element name, so a translator who reasons about the placeholder, as several have in past sprints, will write a sentence about a node. 'the reason given' also leaves the giver unnamed on a page with two engines.
readings: no answer, and the code the solver reported is {id} (intended)
no answer, and the element responsible is {id}
no answer, and the reason we gave is {id}
entries.resolution: English: 'No answer. The code reported was {id}.' Renaming the placeholder to {code} would be better still, but that is a code change and belongs to the task, not to the sprint.

entries.complaint: low: The four state words (Passing, Failing, Design issue, No answer) are present participles or fragments with no subject, and 'Passing' in particular reads as passing THROUGH as readily as meeting a criterion. Worth noting separately: ffStateText() is defined at js/looped-network.js line 27619 and is called from nowhere, and lpn_ff_col_result appears in Looped-Network.php's pageConfig but in no renderer. These five keys currently reach no screen, so the sprint would pay 5 x 26 translations for text nobody sees.
readings: meets the criteria (intended)
passing through, in transit
acceptable or adequate, i.e. only just passing
entries.resolution: Decide reachability BEFORE the sprint: either wire ffStateText() and lpn_ff_col_result into the table, or hold the five keys back from this batch. If they ship, propose 'Pass', 'Fail', 'Design issue', 'No answer' as noun-form verdicts parallel with the Failure modes cells.
